source: Inman on Real REMAX, Compass Q3 2026 earnings; Freddie Mac

headline: Real REMAX plans
for a *tougher 2027*
slides.sub: Its CEO told investors the company is preparing for another very challenging year.
slides.fig_caption: Drop in U.S. existing-home sales the company assumes for 2027

slides.label: years since sales would have been that low, *per its CFO*
slides.body: The outlook also assumes average home prices fall 3% to 4%. The CEO said recent rate increases pushed recovery back. Freddie Mac's 30-year average is 7.18%, up from 6.22% a year ago.

slides.label: agents offboarded at Real in *the past two months*
slides.body: Another 300 to 400 are under review. October exits included 500-plus agents removed for unpaid dues or expired licenses. Real still ended Q3 with 36,610 agents, up 21% from a year earlier.

slides.title: Leaner, with a *higher bar*
points: Real REMAX is winding down Motto Mortgage: 104 of 151 offices have closed since the end of August.
Combined staff headcount is down more than 14%, or over 150 positions, as functions consolidate.
Separately, Compass is raising minimum production requirements for incoming agents by *30%*.

slides.title: Don't budget for a *rebound*
slides.body: This is one company's planning assumption, not a certainty. But it shows how big operators are preparing. If 2027 stays slow, your production and your own pipeline matter more than the market.
